Description - BoxEvents

Uploads client events. The client sends a small fixed set of product events whenever they occur (Observed; this corrects the earlier reading "GUI statistics, off by default"):

  • shutdown = poweroff, suspend or quit: the after-transfers action ran out its countdown (sent 1 s before the action);
  • detected.defaultplayer = 0 together with settings.defaultplayer = 1/0: start-up check when ChomikBox was the default player and lost that role, with the user's answer;
  • settings.defaultplayer = 1: ChomikBox made the default player in Settings;
  • settings.autostart = true/false: autostart changed in Settings.

There is no opt-out and no [guistats] gate. Values are sent as text (bool true/false, int decimal). While logged out the events are queued as name=value; in [proto-box] box-events and flushed after the next successful Auth.

Verified live: an empty list (empty-events) and two real events with values the client itself sends (real-event-names: settings.autostart=false, settings.defaultplayer=0) both give status Ok. Whether the server stores the events: Unknown.

When the client sends it: whenever one of its product events occurs; timestamp is always 0; flagged :noRelog.

Routing. The path item declares the server http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=, so this operation resolves to http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/BoxEvents. WCF ignores the query string and dispatches only on the SOAPAction header (verified live). The real client posts to the bare http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc; both URLs reach the same operation. A path suffix (.svc/BoxEvents) does not work (a:DestinationUnreachable, see soapRestStylePath).

Wire format. POST with Content-Type: text/xml;charset=utf-8 (exact client bytes, no space; the server answers text/xml; charset=utf-8) and SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/BoxEvents (unquoted). Body: SOAP 1.1 envelope, UTF-8, no indentation, parameters in the documented order (WCF silently drops out-of-order parameters). The client gzips the body (Content-Encoding: gzip).

Path notes

SOAP operation BoxEvents. The path-level server makes the URL routable: WCF dispatches on SOAPAction and ignores the ?op=/BoxEvents query.

WCF dispatch key. The client sends it unquoted (SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/BoxEvents); a quoted value works too. Missing or unknown actions give a:ActionNotSupported.

http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/BoxEvents
Content-Encodingheaderoptionalstring one of "gzip"

Present when the body is gzip-compressed ([network] soap-use-gzip=true in the default config; zlib level -1, windowBits 31). Accepted by the service (Auth/success vs Auth/success-uncompressed-request).

Request - body and examples

Body required.

SOAP 1.1 request envelope for BoxEvents (media type text/xml, charset UTF-8).

Body text/xml

Schema

Schema BoxEventsRequestEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required BoxEventsRequestEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 request envelope for BoxEvents: <s:Envelope><s:Body><BoxEvents xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl/">…. No SOAP header is ever sent; xmlns:i is declared on the operation element only when a nil value is present.

    • @s:encodingStyle string optional = "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/encoding/" namespace http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

      SOAP 1.1 encodingStyle attribute. The real client always writes it; the service accepts the envelope with or without it.

    • <s:Body> object required

      Exactly one operation element; no other content (this also makes the per-operation envelopes mutually exclusive).

      • <BoxEvents> object required BoxEventsRequest xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

        Operation element BoxEvents in http://chomikuj.pl/ (trailing slash is mandatory: with http://chomikuj.pl the parameters are not matched, see Service/wrong-operation-namespace).

        • <token> string required Token

          Session token. Always the first child.

        • <timestamp> string optional nullable (i:nil)

          Timestamp; the server type is string. The client always sends 0.

        • <events> list optional

          Events (Event items), queued while logged out and sent in one call.

          • <Event> object optional nullable (i:nil) repeated BoxEvent

            One client event (TeamSolutions.Chomik.Library.DAO.ChomikBox.Event). Names sent by the client (Observed; the client sends no others): shutdown (poweroff/suspend/quit), detected.defaultplayer (0), settings.defaultplayer (0/1), settings.autostart (true/false). Queued as name=value; in [proto-box] box-events while logged out and flushed after Auth.

            • <name> string optional nullable (i:nil)

              Event name (see the list above).

            • <value> string optional nullable (i:nil)

              Event value as text (true/false, decimal integers, or the shutdown mode).

Responses - 200, 500

200

SOAP response envelope. HTTP 200 is used for every service-level outcome, including errors: check BoxEventsResult/status. Compressed (Content-Encoding: gzip) when the request accepts gzip.

Schema text/xml

Schema BoxEventsResponseEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required BoxEventsResponseEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 response envelope for BoxEvents: <s:Envelope><s:Body><BoxEventsResponse xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl/"><BoxEventsResult …>.

    • <s:Body> object required

      Exactly one response element; no other content.

      • <BoxEventsResponse> object required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/
        • <BoxEventsResult> object required StatusResult

          Result element; declares xmlns:i (XML Schema instance, for i:nil) and xmlns:a.

          • <a:status> string required Status xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Outcome of the call. The client accepts only Ok; BadToken triggers a re-login, anything else is an error.

            7 values
            • "Ok" Success. The only value the client treats as success.
            • "BadToken" Unknown, logged-out or otherwise invalid token. The client re-authenticates (Auth) once per message (message-relog-count=1) and resends the message with the new token; session-bound messages are dropped.
            • "Forbidden" Auth: user name does not exist. The client shows the credentials dialog.
            • "PermissionError" Auth: wrong password for an existing user. The client shows the credentials dialog.
            • "Error" Generic failure. Usually carries a reason in errorMessage (e.g. EmptyName, NameExistsAtDestination); FolderFiles with an unknown disposition returns Error with errorMessage nil (FolderFiles/invalid-disposition).
            • "NotEmptyOrNotExistsFolder" RemoveFolder with force=false on a folder that contains files, or on an unknown/removed folder id.
            • "WrongDisposition" FolderFiles: the disposition is a known value but not allowed for this call (download).
          • <a:errorMessage> string required nullable (i:nil) ErrorMessage xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Error detail for status=Error; nil otherwise.

500 SoapFault

WCF SOAP fault (HTTP 500, Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8, not compressed). Possible for every SOAP operation: an empty or malformed body gives a:InternalServiceFault, an undeserialisable value a:DeserializationFailed, an unknown or missing SOAPAction a:ActionNotSupported. Operations with an operation-specific captured fault document it inline instead.

Schema text/xml

Schema SoapFaultEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required SoapFaultEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 fault envelope (HTTP 500, Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8, never gzip-compressed).

    • <s:Body> object required
      • <s:Fault> object required SoapFault

        The fault.

        • <faultcode> string required no namespace

          Qualified fault code with its own namespace declaration on the element: a:InternalServiceFault and a:DeserializationFailed (a = http://schemas.microsoft.com/net/2005/12/windowscommunicationfoundation/dispatcher), a:ActionNotSupported and a:DestinationUnreachable (a = http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2005/05/addressing/none).

        • <faultstring> object required no namespace

          Human-readable message. DeserializationFailed names the parameter and CLR type, which is how the contract was established.

          • @xml:lang string required namespace http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace

            Language of the message (en-US).

          • text content string required

            Message text.

Client vs live - discrepancies

Where the client's expected behaviour and the live service disagree, the spec follows the live behaviour (x-discrepancies):

  • The client sends timestamp as the int constant 0; the server parameter is a string (the client's 0 is a valid string).

Security notes - findings that concern BoxEvents

  • C-09 Info Usage data stats{isUploading, isPlaying, isDownloading, panelSelectedTab, animation} rides on every CheckEvents poll. BoxEvents is not off by default: it sends fixed events whenever they occur (shutdown = poweroff/suspend/quit, detected.defaultplayer, settings.defaultplayer, settings.autostart).

From x-security-notes in the spec. Ratings and scope are explained on Security & privacy.
